[image: It’s time for a breakup. 24 years is enough, and it’s time to stop the rise in crime. In 2019, Albany passed sweeping bail reform, eliminating cash bail for most misdemeanors and nonviolent felonies. When Governor Hochul pushed for changes in 2022 amid rising concerns about public safety, my opponent Liz Krueger defended the law and argued that rising crime was not caused by bail reform. Six years later, New Yorkers are still living with the consequences of policies that make it harder to keep repeat offenders off our streets. I’m running to amend the law, restore greater judicial discretion and give judges the ability to consider public safety and repeat offenses when making pretrial decisions. Manhattan deserves laws that protect the rights of the accused and the safety of the public. After 24 years with the same representation it's enough, let's end the Neglect. [image: I’m honored to have been invited to present at Weill Cornell Medicine’s David Rogers Health Policy Colloquium. Healthcare has always been close to my heart. I spent 15 years in the industry, working with physicians and hospital systems and training doctors. I saw firsthand how bureaucracy and policy can make it harder for physicians to practice medicine and ultimately impact the care patients receive. Now, two of my worlds are colliding: healthcare and public policy. I’m especially excited to speak with the next generation of physicians about how healthcare policy becomes law and how clinicians can help shape it. Doctors on the front lines see what works and what doesn’t, and their voices should have a meaningful path into policymaking. As a State Senator, I would work to make sure those voices are heard in Albany and that good ideas can move through the right channels to become better policy.
